newsitem.title: USA: Most IMM currency futures end short session lower.
newsitem.headline: Most IMM currency futures end short session lower.

text.p: IMM currency futures ended an abbreviated trading session mostly lower but largely in the upper portion of daily ranges.
IMM currencies closed early on Friday at 1200 CDT/1700 GMT and will remain shut on Monday, September 2, for the U.S. Labor Day holiday.
Yen sagged again near the close as one bank was seen selling 2,000 September contracts, traders said.
Currencies had nearly erased morning losses after stronger than expected U.S. economic data, statistics that shoved U.S. equity and Treasury markets to steep losses.
In particular, the August Chicago purchasing managers index jumped to 60.0, far above forecasts for 51.9.

July U.S. factory orders rose 1.8 percent, above average forecasts for up 1.0 percent. And paying subscribers reported that the University of Michigan final August consumer sentiment index rose to 95.3 from 94.7 final in July.
Traders said the data sparked a rise in currencies only because the figures slammed U.S. Treasury and stock markets lower on revived speculation that the Federal Reserve might need to tighten credit.
The Federal Open Market Committee meets next on Sept 24.
July U.S. personal income rose 0.1 percent and spending gained 0.2 percent, close to forecasts, and had muted effect.

Marks had built losses overnight after a Bundesbank spokesman confirmed that the central bank's president, Hans Tietmeyer, said in an interview with a German news agency that U.S. economic fundamentals speak for a slightly higher dollar.

But the contract held support near $0.6741 or 1.4850 spot and began whittling losses. It also was seen as likely to stay strong on crosses, as the market remains skeptical that some nations, including France, will meet European monetary union criteria, despite officials' recent remarks to the contrary.
French President Jacques Chirac meets in Bonn on Sunday with German Chancellor Helmut Kohl and possibly will discuss European Monetary Union issues.
French Prime Minister Alain Juppe on Friday reaffirmed France's commitment to EMU targets and said he did not expect the Maastricht treaty criteria to be revised.
Chirac made similar comments on Thursday.
Yen, however, sagged again on perceptions that Japan's economy is still soggy, especially after Wednesday's unexpectedly weak Tankan report erased ideas that Japanese rates might rise soon.

Swiss francs fell when Swiss National Bank added liquidity and reportedly conducted currency swaps that brought down Swiss short-term rates. SNB chief economist Georg Rich said SNB's recent liquidity-adding did not pose an inflation threat.
Traders saw no response when Federal Reserve chairman Alan Greenspan said price stability is within reach of major nations and reiterated his definition of price stability.

Sept yen fell $0.000047 to $0.009200, marks fell $0.0017 to $0.6762, Swiss fr fell $0.0050 to $0.8337, pound up $0.0038 at $1.5618, Can dollar off $0.0009 at $0.7314, Aussie dollar fell $0.0024 to $0.7890, Mex peso slid $0.000775 to $0.130550. --Derivatives Desk 312-408-8750 E-mail:derivatives@reuters.com
